title: Shopping & money
goal: Ask prices, bargain, choose 'this one' or 'that one', ask for sizes and colours, and pay.
intro:
From glittering malls to street stalls, shopping in India is an experience — and in markets, a bit of friendly bargaining (मोल-भाव) is expected. This unit gives you money, clothes and shopping words, and the phrases to haggle with a smile.

Grammar: the 'this/that' words change before postpositions (**इस** दुकान में 'in this shop'), the magic suffix **वाला** ('the … one'), and how to ask prices.

Bring the price down a bit, please.
Do you have this in a bigger size?

OK, I'll take it. (lit. give it)

grammar.title: This and that before postpositions: इस, उस, इन, उन
grammar.body:
Like nouns, the demonstratives change before a postposition (the oblique case):

यह 'this' → **इस**: इस दुकान में 'in this shop'
वह 'that' → **उस**: उस आदमी से 'from that man'
ये 'these' → **इन**: इन जूतों का दाम 'the price of these shoes'
वे 'those' → **उन**: उन लोगों को 'to those people'

The same forms, joined to the postposition, mean 'it/him/her': **इसका** 'its/his', **इसमें** 'in this/it', **उससे** 'from him/her/it', **इनको / इन्हें** 'to them'.

You already know the dative forms उसे and इसे — they are short for उसको / इसको.

examples.roman: is kamīz kā dām kyā hai?

examples.en: These shoes don't come in my size.
Does this come in another colour?

grammar.title: वाला: 'the … one' and 'the person who…'
grammar.body:
**वाला** (वाली, वाले — it agrees like an -ā adjective) is one of the handiest words in Hindi. After an adjective or a demonstrative it means **'the … one'**:

यह **वाला** 'this one' · वह **वाली** 'that one (f)' · लाल **वाला** 'the red one' · सस्ते **वाले** 'the cheap ones'

After a noun it means **'the person/thing connected with'**: चाय**वाला** 'tea seller', सब्ज़ी**वाला** 'vegetable seller', दिल्ली**वाले** 'Delhiites', दूध**वाला** 'milkman'.

After an oblique infinitive it means **'about to'**: ट्रेन जाने **वाली** है 'the train is about to leave' (more in Unit 17).

examples.native: नीली वाली साड़ी कितने की है?
examples.roman: nīlī vālī sāṛī kitne kī hai?
examples.en: How much is the blue sari?

grammar.title: Asking and giving prices
grammar.body:
Ask **कितने का है?** — literally 'of how many (rupees) is it?' The का agrees with the item: **कितने का** (m), **कितने की** (f), **कितने के** (pl): यह जूता कितने का है? यह साड़ी कितने की है? ये आम कितने के हैं?

Answer the same way: **सौ रुपये का है** / **पाँच सौ की है**. You can also just ask **कितना हुआ?** or **कितने हुए?** 'how much does it come to?' — and कुल 'total'.

Prices per unit: पचास रुपये किलो '50 rupees a kilo' (no postposition needed), बीस रुपये का एक '20 rupees each'.

dialogue.title: Bargaining for a kurta
dialogue.setting: Emma is at a market stall in Jaipur looking at cotton kurtas.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.en: Come in, madam! What would you like?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: मुझे एक कुर्ता चाहिए। यह नीला वाला कितने का है?
lines.roman: mujhe ek kurtā chāhiye. yah nīlā vālā kitne kā hai?
lines.en: I'd like a kurta. How much is this blue one?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: यह बहुत अच्छा कपड़ा है, मैडम। सिर्फ़ बारह सौ रुपये।
lines.roman: yah bahut achchhā kapṛā hai, maiḍam. sirf bārah sau rupaye.
lines.en: This is very good cloth, madam. Only 1,200 rupees.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: बारह सौ? बहुत महँगा है! कुछ कम कीजिए।
lines.roman: bārah sau? bahut mahaṃgā hai! kuchh kam kījiye.
lines.en: 1,200? That's too expensive! Bring it down a bit.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: नहीं मैडम, इतने में नहीं होगा। आठ सौ, आख़िरी दाम।
lines.roman: nahīṃ maiḍam, itne meṃ nahīṃ hogā. āṭh sau, āxirī dām.
lines.en: No madam, can't do it for that. Eight hundred, final price.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: सात सौ। और क्या इसमें बड़ा साइज़ है?
lines.roman: sāt sau. aur kyā ismeṃ baṛā sāiz hai?
lines.en: Seven hundred. And do you have it in a bigger size?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: हाँ, यह लीजिए — बड़ा साइज़। ठीक है, सात सौ।
lines.roman: hāṃ, yah lījiye — baṛā sāiz. ṭhīk hai, sāt sau.
lines.en: Yes, here you go — the bigger size. Alright, seven hundred.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.en: Not card, but UPI is fine.

culture: Bargaining is normal in markets, with street vendors and auto drivers — but **not** in malls, supermarkets, chemists or shops with printed prices (MRP, 'maximum retail price'). Keep it friendly: smile, offer about half, and meet somewhere in the middle; walking away politely often brings a better offer. Today most payments, even at tiny stalls, are made by scanning a QR code with a phone (UPI), so carrying small change matters less than it used to — but खुले पैसे are still handy for autos and tips.

tip.title: कितने का? — how much is it?
tip.body:
- Ask **कितने का है?** for a masculine item, **कितने की है?** for a feminine one, **कितने के हैं?** for plurals.
- Answer the same way: पाँच सौ रुपये **का** है (कुर्ता), दो हज़ार **की** है (साड़ी).
- Or just ask **कितना हुआ?** 'how much is that?'
tip.pattern: item + कितने का / की / के + है?

sentences.en: It's five hundred rupees. (a masculine item)

sentences.native: यह साड़ी दो हज़ार की है।
sentences.roman: yah sāṛī do hazār kī hai.

sentences.native: यह किताब तीन सौ की है।
sentences.roman: yah kitāb tīn sau kī hai.

tip.title: सस्ता, सस्ती, सस्ते
tip.body:
- Adjectives ending in **-आ** agree with the thing: **महँगा** (m), **महँगी** (f), **महँगे** (m pl).
- साड़ी is feminine → साड़ी **महँगी** है; कुर्ता is masculine → कुर्ता **महँगा** है.
- In markets, bargaining is normal: say **बहुत महँगा है!** and ask for the **आख़िरी दाम**.

sentences.en: Vegetables are cheap at the market.
Delhi is a very expensive city.

sentences.native: चाय यहाँ सस्ती है, बीस रुपये।
sentences.roman: chāy yahāṃ sastī hai, bīs rupaye.
sentences.en: Tea is cheap here — twenty rupees.
Can I get a bit of a discount?

sentences.native: मुझे मोल-भाव करना पसंद नहीं है।
sentences.roman: mujhe mol-bhāv karnā pasand nahīṃ hai.

tip.title: वाला — 'the … one'
tip.body:
- After an adjective, **वाला** means 'the … one': **लाल वाला** 'the red one', **यह वाला** 'this one'.
- It agrees like an -आ adjective: **वाला** (m), **वाली** (f), **वाले** (pl).
- After a noun it means 'the person who sells…': **चायवाला** 'tea seller'.

sentences.native: मुझे वह नीली वाली कमीज़ दिखाइए।
sentences.roman: mujhe vah nīlī vālī kamīz dikhāiye.
sentences.en: Show me that blue shirt, please.

sentences.native: यह वाला जूता कितने का है?
sentences.roman: yah vālā jūtā kitne kā hai?

sentences.en: Show me the black shoes, please.
The red one or the green one? (a feminine item)
Show me the big ones, please.

sentences.native: पीली वाली साड़ी ज़्यादा सुंदर है।
sentences.roman: pīlī vālī sāṛī zyādā sundar hai.

lessons.title: In this shop, in that size

tip.title: इस, उस — this / that before a postposition
tip.body:
- Before **में, से, का, पर, को**, यह becomes **इस** and वह becomes **उस**: **इस** दुकान में, **उस** आदमी से.
- Plural: ये → **इन**, वे → **उन**.
- Joined up they mean 'it / him / her': **इसमें** 'in this', **इसका** 'its', **उससे** 'from him/her'.

sentences.roman: us thaile meṃ merī kitābeṃ haiṃ.

sentences.roman: ise badal dījiye, yah chhoṭā hai.
sentences.en: Please exchange this, it's too small.

sentences.native: क्या मैं यह पहनकर देख सकता हूँ?
sentences.roman: kyā maiṃ yah pahankar dekh saktā hūṃ?

sentences.native: मैं बाज़ार से सब्ज़ी ख़रीदती हूँ।
sentences.roman: maiṃ bāzār se sabzī xarīdtī hūṃ.

sentences.roman: mere pās khule paise nahīṃ haiṃ, sirf kārḍ hai.
sentences.en: I don't have change, only a card.

sentences.native: ठीक है, यह वाला दे दीजिए।
sentences.roman: ṭhīk hai, yah vālā de dījiye.
